column2: Retain the assembly in Jerusalem of all the named administrative and military groups, including rulers of judges and courses attending the king's person. Do not replace judges with tribes or add royal sons and eunuchs from another witness.

Retain David standing in the assembly, addressing brethren and people, the ark's house of rest and a standing place for the Lord's feet. The feet image and prepared dwelling materials remain without importing a different posture or architectural gloss.
Retain the building prohibition, the name called upon the house and the reasons warrior and shed blood. Ordinary you addresses David within the quoted divine speech.
Retain divine choice of David, royal power in Judah, his father's house and his own selection among its sons. The nested choices are not collapsed into a simple tribe-to-king statement.
Retain the parenthesis about many sons and Solomon chosen for the throne of the Lord's kingdom over Israel. This throne designation is not harmonized to David's throne in chapter 29.
Retain Solomon building God's house and singular court, chosen as son with God as Father. Do not pluralize court to match another building description.
Retain the conditional lasting kingdom, strength to observe commandments and judgments and as on this day. The condition is not removed to make an unconditional royal guarantee.

Retain the whole assembly, God's ears, observing and seeking all commandments and inheritance of the good land transmitted to their sons. The speech's plural audience precedes the singular address to Solomon.

Retain And now, fathers plural, whole heart and willing soul, examination of every heart and knowledge of every thought. Seeking and forsaking have their respective outcomes; ordinary you addresses Solomon, not God.
Retain attention to divine choice, building a sanctuary and the two imperatives be strong and act. The English does not append a promised outcome to this brief charge.
Retain pattern of temple, houses, zakcho, upper rooms, inner storerooms and house of propitiation. No porch is substituted for temple, and the opaque architectural term remains visible.
column3: Zakcho and the precise room designated by house of propitiation need lexical review; no accepted architectural identification is claimed.

column2: Retain the pattern in his spirit, courts and surrounding chambers and both categories of storerooms. Lowercase spirit preserves the inherited uncertainty about its relation to David and divine inspiration.
column3: The antecedent of his and the sense of spirit require review; verse 19's divine-hand wording does not by itself settle this pronoun.

column2: Retain lodgings of priestly and Levitical courses, all service work and storerooms for worship vessels. The repeated house-of-the-Lord phrases retain their distinct functions.
Retain the measure of weight and both gold and silver objects. He gave is supplied from the surrounding giving construction; no specific amount is invented.
Retain the selected short statement giving the weight of lampstands and lamps. Do not import expanded material-by-material or individual-lamp specifications absent from this unit.
Retain presentation tables, each golden table and silver ones likewise. No silver table is omitted to conform to an expected sanctuary inventory.
Retain meat hooks, libation vessels, golden bowls, gold/silver weights and kephphoure of each weight. The selected borrowed form is not silently identified with another vessel category.
column3: Kephphoure remains untranslated and unapproved; its referent and attachment require lexical and witness review.

column2: Retain incense altar of tested gold, its weight and the cherubim chariot pattern with spread wings shading the covenant ark. Do not suppress the chariot image as an architectural difficulty.

Retain David giving Solomon everything in writing from the Lord's hand according to understanding received about the pattern. The selected third-person narrative is not converted into a first-person quotation.
column3: The exact relation of divine-hand writing to David's received understanding remains open; no physical writing mechanism is asserted.

column2: Retain strength, courage and action, both fear prohibitions, the Lord my God with Solomon and no abandonment until all the work is finished. Until does not imply that abandonment necessarily follows completion.

Retain priestly and Levitical courses, willing skilled workers, rulers and all the people for Solomon's words. Ready supplies the elliptical availability, not a claim that every person is already on site.
Retain Solomon as the chosen one, young and tender, and the greatness of work for God rather than a human. The one does not become an added claim that Solomon is David's only son.

Retain all strength in preparation, five basic materials and the distinct stone descriptions, including soom, filling stones and much Parian marble. Do not replace the entire stone list with a generic precious-stones phrase.
column3: Soom, filling stones and the identification of parion as Parian marble remain provisional lexical decisions.

column2: Retain personal delight, separately acquired gold and silver and an additional gift beyond prior preparations for the holy house. The personally acquired supplies remain distinct from the preceding general stock.
column3: In addition interprets eis hypsos contextually; its exact sense of height, magnitude or extra provision requires review.

column2: Retain 3,000 talents of gold from Souphir and 7,000 of tested silver to coat the sanctuary walls. No material or amount is changed to reconcile another inventory.
Retain by craftsmen's hand as continuation, then the question of willing hands filled for the Lord today. Do not import a longer gold-for-gold and silver-for-silver clause from another witness.
column3: Fill his hands preserves the consecration or offering image; its precise application here remains open.

column2: Retain every listed leadership group and their eagerness, including work overseers and royal stewards. No single official is made the sole donor.

Retain 5,000 gold talents plus 10,000 gold coins, 10,000 silver talents, 18,000 bronze talents and 100,000 iron talents. Gold coins is the inherited nominal reading; no unexpressed daric denomination is specified.
Retain those possessing a stone giving it to the storerooms through Jiiel the Gersoni. The selected singular stone is not expanded into a named gem category.
Retain the repeated eagerness, full heart and both people's and David's joy. The cause of rejoicing remains voluntary readiness, not merely the size of the receipts.

Retain David's public blessing, Thou, God of Israel, our Father and everlasting duration. The nominative father apposition is retained as address to God rather than silently attached to indeclinable Israel as an ancestor.

Retain the five praise nouns, divine rule of all heavenly and earthly things and every king and nation shaken before God. Do not replace the final selected clause with a familiar Thine-is-the-kingdom formula.
column3: Glory renders kauchema here, unlike boasting in 16:27 and doxa in the next verse. This lexical and stylistic difference remains under review rather than treated as settled equivalence.

column2: Retain wealth and glory from God, rule over all, Ruler of every rule, strength and dominion in His hand and the Almighty making all things great and strong. Repeated hand and all expressions remain in direct Thy/Thou address.
Retain thanksgiving and praise of the name of Thy glory. The first-person plural verbs remain ordinary English within direct divine address.
column3: The glory rendering of kauchesis shares the unresolved boasting/glory question of verse 11; no identity with doxa is assumed.

column2: Retain the two questions, collective strength for willing giving and the claim that all is God's and the gift comes from His own. Thine/Thee address God while we remains first person.
Retain resident strangers and sojourners like the fathers, days as a shadow and no endurance. Do not substitute no hope or an assurance of permanence for the selected negative expression.
column3: The sense of hypomone as duration, remaining or endurance here remains a lexical question; no endurance is provisional.

column2: Retain singular I prepared, the holy-name house purpose and all abundance from God's hand belonging to Him. Do not change I to we to align the collective giving around it.

Retain divine examination of hearts and love of righteousness, simplicity of David's heart and the present people's joyful willingness. Thy and Thee address God; the people's giving is reported from David's observation.

Retain Abraham, Isaac and Israel as our fathers, these things preserved in the thought of the people's heart and their hearts directed toward God. Singular collective heart and later plural hearts remain distinct.
Retain a good heart for Solomon, commandments, testimonies and ordinances, and completion of God's house. Do not replace good with perfect or add David's preparation clause from another text.

Retain the command to bless, the assembly's blessing, bent knees and prostration before both Lord and king. The same verb's two recipients remain without adding an explanation that resolves the nature of each act.

Retain explicit David as sacrificer, the day after the first day, 1,000 calves, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs, libations and abundant sacrifices for all Israel. The repeated sacrifice language is not removed or assigned to a different actor.
Retain joyful eating and drinking, making Solomon king a second time and anointing him for the Lord as king and Sadok for priesthood. The second enthronement is explicit, not an added again.
Retain David's throne, Solomon accepted with favor and all Israel obeying. Do not replace David with the Lord or turn the passive acceptance into an unqualified prosperity claim.
column3: The agent of acceptance is unexpressed; the English does not explicitly identify it as God or the people.

column2: Retain rulers, powerful men and all sons of King David submitting to Solomon. His father refers to Solomon's father David, not a new figure.
Retain the Lord's extraordinary exaltation before all Israel and unprecedented royal glory. The selected comparison is any earlier king, without a newly added in-Israel restriction.
Retain David son of Jessai reigning over Israel, with the duration continuing in the next stored unit. No full stop or added time figure interrupts the sentence.
Retain forty years, seven in Chebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem. Do not add the six months from an earlier reign notice or change the total.
Retain good old age, fullness of days, wealth and glory, and Solomon succeeding his father. The death notice is not expanded into an account of burial absent here.

Retain earlier and later deeds in the records of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet and Gad the seer. The three designations and sources remain distinct without identifying surviving books beyond the text.
Retain all his kingdom and dominion and the times affecting him, Israel and every earthly kingdom. The final clause completes the record notice rather than adding a new historical event.
